mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 3.0% signals an active monetary easing cycle that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.8% signals labor market tightening that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.8%, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both rising) fails to predict positive 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) in more than 50% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), the Federal Reserve's tightening response depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) above 115.0 indicates expanding manufacturing output, which typically precedes positive short-term equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth is not associated with positive 5-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.02) in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized) signals robust economic expansion that drives corporate earnings momentum, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 35% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS > 100k monthly) and unemployment decline (UNRATE < 5.0%) signal labor market strength that boosts consumer confidence and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to predict positive 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) in more than 50% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
